pages.text: An enzyme turns substrate over fastest when it is saturated. Its saturation is v/Vmax = Sⁿ/(K_appⁿ + Sⁿ): n = 1 for an ordinary enzyme (Michaelis-Menten), more for a cooperative one (Hill), and an inhibitor raises K_app = K_m(1 + I/K_i). Too much substrate chokes the enzyme; too much enzyme clumps.
$(thing)Set$(): Substrate, Enzyme dose.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Temperature: the saturation varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): Too much substrate: it chokes the enzyme; Too much enzyme: it clumps.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): More enzyme, well saturated, is faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Apparent K: K_app = K_m(1 + I/K_i)$(br)Saturation: v/Vmax = Sⁿ/(K_appⁿ + Sⁿ)
